root_idea.summary: The root centers on slenderness, fineness, and tapering or paring, with the divining arrow as a principal lexical branch.
root_idea.development: From the idea of a slender or pared form, the lexicon develops meanings for arrows, cutting and shaping, smallness, pendulous appendages, and physically slight forms; the arrow branch also yields the conventional instrument of divination.

senses.definition: A divining arrow: an arrow used in sortilege to seek an indication of what one should do or what has been allotted to one.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic form is the plural أَزْلَام. The arrows were traditionally marked with commands, prohibitions, or left blank, and drawn to decide whether to proceed with an affair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cut off the nose, or another projecting or prominent part.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The extension to anything projecting is reported as an apparent or assumed figurative use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a gift small or scant in amount; مُزَلَّمٌ describes a gift that is small or scanted.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb is explained as a figurative extension of cutting something away.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fill a watering-trough, tank, or vessel.
To cut or pare an arrow and shape it evenly, supplely, and with good proportion and workmanship; by extension, to round or properly prepare a millstone or stone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The principal construction is with an arrow; the same shaping action is also applied to millstones and stones.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cut off someone's head or extirpate the nose.
The slender legs of a wild ox or cow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a figurative comparison of the legs to slender arrows.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A strong, light, or active boy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The description is explained as likening the boy to a slender arrow.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cloven hoof, especially that of an ox or similar animal, or the projection behind it.
The hyrax, one of the animals called وَبْرٌ.

In the idiom هُوَ العَبْدُ زَلْمَةً, a person whose appearance or conformation is that of a slave; by extension, one who is truly or completely a slave, and figuratively a low, ignoble, or mean person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression is proverbial and is used in disapproval. Some authorities interpret زَلْمَةً as meaning “truly” or “in reality.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: A pendulous wattle hanging externally from a goat's throat; a she-goat may have two such appendages.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A similar appendage of the ear is distinguished by the form with ن.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having the end of the ear cut, with a portion left hanging; of a goat, having the two wattles called زَلَمَتَانِ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to certain camels, sheep, and goats; the feminine form is زَلْمَاءُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The male mountain-goat, or the female mountain-goat in the corresponding feminine form.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression الأَزْلَمُ الجَذَعُ and its feminine counterpart الزَّلْمَاءُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hard or rigorous time or fortune, marked by trials and deaths.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional figurative expression for a period whose course brings destruction or inescapable hardship.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The female of a hawk species.
Well pared, proportioned, shaped, even, and supple.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to an arrow; the feminine form is also applied to a staff.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Short or cropped in the tail.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An assumed figurative extension of something having its projecting part cut away.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To give someone bad or inadequate nourishment, so that the person's body becomes small.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The meaning is an assumed figurative extension associated with making something small.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Small in body, or badly fed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective may describe one rendered small by poor feeding or simply one who is badly fed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of slight, light, short, or active build; of a woman, not tall.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a man in the masculine form and to a woman in the feminine form; some descriptions also include elegance or cleverness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a horse, middling or moderate in build.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression concerns the horse's overall conformation.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The small or scanted gift is covered together with the corresponding verb.

cautions: The Quranic form is plural أَزْلَام; the public headword is normalized to the singular زَلَمٌ. زُلَمٌ is also recorded as a vocalic variant.
The Quranic usage concerns divining arrows. The lexical evidence reports, but rejects, an identification of أَزْلَام with the arrows used in the game of maysir.
